indication.text: Adempas is a sGC stimulator indicated in adults for (1) persistent/recurrent CTEPH (WHO Group 4) after surgical treatment or inoperable CTEPH, to improve exercise capacity and WHO functional class; and (2) pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1), to improve exercise capacity, WHO functional class and to delay clinical worsening.

citations.quote: Adempas is indicated for the treatment of adults with persistent/recurrent chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), (WHO Group 4) after surgical treatment, or inoperable CTEPH, to improve exercise capacity and WHO functional class [see *Clinical Studies (14.1)*].
Adempas is indicated for the treatment of adults with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), (WHO Group 1), to improve exercise capacity, WHO functional class and to delay clinical worsening.

target_moa.text: Riociguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), the receptor for nitric oxide (NO); it sensitizes sGC to endogenous NO and directly stimulates sGC independently of NO, increasing intracellular cGMP, which regulates vascular tone, proliferation, fibrosis and inflammation, producing vasodilation.

citations.quote: Riociguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), an enzyme in the cardiopulmonary system and the receptor for nitric oxide (NO). When NO binds to sGC, the enzyme catalyzes synthesis of the signaling molecule cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP). Intracellular cGMP plays an important role in regulating processes that influence vascular tone, proliferation, fibrosis and inflammation. P

- Pharmacologic class. Riociguat is a small-molecule agonist of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), which is the receptor for nitric oxide (NO).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥3% more than placebo, pooled n=490 vs 214): headache (27% vs 18%), dyspepsia/gastritis (21% vs 8%), dizziness (20% vs 13%), nausea (14% vs 11%), diarrhea (12% vs 8%), hypotension (10% vs 4%), and vomiting (10% vs 7%). Serious bleeding occurred in 2.4% of Adempas patients vs 0% placebo.

detail.text: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Do not administer Adempas to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm; females of reproductive potential must exclude pregnancy before, monthly during, and 1 month after treatment and prevent pregnancy with acceptable contraception; available for females only through the Adempas REMS Program.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY
- Do not administer Adempas to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm. (4.1, 5.1, 8.1)
For all female patients, Adempas is available only through a restricted program called the Adempas Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) Program [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.2)*].

detail.text: Females can only receive Adempas through the Adempas REMS Program, a restricted distribution program, to mitigate the risk of teratogenicity; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified, all females must enroll, and females of reproductive potential must comply with pregnancy testing and contraception requirements.

citations.quote: Females can only receive Adempas through the Adempas REMS Program, a restricted distribution program [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.1)].

summary.text: Riociguat is a first-in-class new molecular entity reviewed under priority review and with orphan drug designation; approval was based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies (CHEST-1 in CTEPH and PATENT-1 in PAH), and this was the first approval of a treatment for CTEPH. The application was approved first cycle with a REMS for teratogenicity.

citations.quote: Riociguat is a first-in-class NME that is not currently marketed in the US or in any other country. At the time of the NDA submission, the ATC code had not yet been assigned, but the application had been submitted to WHO.
